title: Integrated network toxicology and experimental validation identify VCAM1 as a candidate molecular link between pyrethroid exposure and keloid.
summary: Random forest, SVM-RFE and LASSO prioritized VCAM1 and FGFR1 from integrated toxicology and keloid gene data. External transcriptomic data and a cell assay supported VCAM1, but this candidate association does not establish that pyrethroids cause keloids or prove the proposed VCAM1–SOCS3 mechanism.
organization: The Second Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University; Shenyang Fifth People’s Hospital; The First Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University; Medical School of Nanjing University

evidence.tested: VCAM1 remained elevated in external transcriptomic cohorts (AUC 0.869); 20 μM cypermethrin exposure for 24 hours increased VCAM1 mRNA in KEL FIB cells. FGFR1 had weaker external support.
evidence.unknown: The evidence supports a candidate molecular link, not causal exposure risk or a validated mechanism; cell testing used one concentration and time.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
